ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, in the equilateral triangle $ABC$, the bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects with the bisector of $\angle ACB$ at point $D$. Through point $D$, line segment $EF$ is drawn parallel to $BC$, intersecting $AB$ at $E$ and $AC$ at $F$, with $EF=4$. What is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in equilateral triangle ABC, EF$\parallel$BC,\\
thus $\angle$AEF=$\angle$ABC=$\angle$AFE=$\angle$ACB=$60^\circ$, and AB=AC=BC,\\
which implies that $\triangle$AEF is also an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore AE=EF=FA=4,\\
resulting in EB=FC,\\
since the bisector of $\angle$ABC intersects with the bisector of $\angle$ACB at point D, and EF$\parallel$BC,\\
it follows that $\angle$EBD=$\angle$DBC=$\angle$EDB=$\angle$FCD=$\angle$FDC=$\angle$DCB=$30^\circ$,\\
hence EB=ED=DF=FC,\\
given EF=4,\\
it leads to EB=ED=DF=FC=2,\\
therefore AB=AC=BC=AE+EB=\boxed{6},

From the text, D is the intersection of the angle bisectors from B and C. In an equilateral triangle, all angle bisectors, medians, altitudes, and perpendicular bisectors coincide, so D is the common center/centroid of ABC. Therefore D lies on the altitude from A to BC and divides that altitude in the ratio AD:DG=2:1, where G is the midpoint of BC; equivalently, D is two-thirds of the way from A down to BC. A line parallel to BC cuts a smaller triangle AEF similar to ABC. The similarity scale equals AD/AG=2/3, so EF/BC=2/3. Since EF=4, solve 4=(2/3)BC, giving BC=6.
